questions.q: Find the critical point(s) of $f(x,y)=x^2+3y^2-4x+6y$.
questions.answer: $f_x=2x-4=0 \Rightarrow x=2$. $f_y=6y+6=0 \Rightarrow y=-1$. Critical point: $(2,-1)$.

questions.q: Find the critical point(s) of $f(x,y)=xy-x^2-y^2$.
questions.answer: $f_x=y-2x=0 \Rightarrow y=2x$. $f_y=x-2y=0 \Rightarrow x=2y$. Substituting: $x=2(2x)=4x \Rightarrow x=0$, so $y=0$. Critical point: $(0,0)$.

sections.heading: Lagrange multipliers: setting up the system

questions.q: Set up the Lagrange multiplier equations to optimize $f(x,y)=xy$ subject to $g(x,y)=x+y-10=0$.
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle y,x\rangle=\lambda\langle1,1\rangle \Rightarrow y=\lambda,\ x=\lambda \Rightarrow x=y$, together with the constraint $x+y=10$.

questions.q: Maximize $f(x,y)=xy$ subject to $x+y=10$.
questions.answer: From the setup above, $x=y$ and $x+y=10 \Rightarrow x=y=5$. Maximum value: $f(5,5)=25$.

questions.q: Minimize $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$ subject to $x+y=4$.
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle2x,2y\rangle=\lambda\langle1,1\rangle \Rightarrow x=y$. With $x+y=4$: $x=y=2$. Minimum value: $f(2,2)=8$.

questions.q: Find the point on the line $x+y=6$ closest to the origin, using Lagrange multipliers on $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$.
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle2x,2y\rangle=\lambda\langle1,1\rangle \Rightarrow x=y$. With $x+y=6$: $x=y=3$. Closest point: $(3,3)$, at distance $\sqrt{9+9}=3\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: Find the critical point(s) of $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2-6x+2y+5$.
questions.answer: $f_x=2x-6=0 \Rightarrow x=3$. $f_y=2y+2=0 \Rightarrow y=-1$. Critical point: $(3,-1)$.

questions.q: Find the critical point(s) of $f(x,y)=x^3-3xy+y^3$.
questions.answer: $f_x=3x^2-3y=0 \Rightarrow y=x^2$. $f_y=-3x+3y^2=0 \Rightarrow x=y^2$. Substituting: $x=(x^2)^2=x^4 \Rightarrow x^4-x=0 \Rightarrow x(x^3-1)=0 \Rightarrow x=0$ or $x=1$. This gives $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$.

questions.q: Classify the critical point $(3,-1)$ of $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2-6x+2y+5$.
Classify the critical points $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ of $f(x,y)=x^3-3xy+y^3$ found above.
A firm's profit from producing $x,y$ units of two goods is $P(x,y)=100x+120y-2x^2-3y^2-2xy$. Find the production levels that maximize profit.
questions.answer: $P_x=100-4x-2y=0 \Rightarrow 2x+y=50$. $P_y=120-6y-2x=0 \Rightarrow x+3y=60$. From the first, $y=50-2x$; substituting: $x+3(50-2x)=60 \Rightarrow -5x=-90 \Rightarrow x=18$, $y=14$. Check: $P_{xx}=-4$, $P_{yy}=-6$, $P_{xy}=-2$; $D=24-4=20>0$ and $P_{xx}<0$, confirming a maximum at $(18,14)$.

sections.heading: Lagrange multipliers with a circular constraint

questions.q: Set up the Lagrange multiplier equations to optimize $f(x,y)=x+y$ subject to $x^2+y^2=8$.
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle1,1\rangle=\lambda\langle2x,2y\rangle \Rightarrow x=y$, together with the constraint $x^2+y^2=8$.

questions.q: Find the maximum and minimum values of $f(x,y)=x+y$ subject to $x^2+y^2=8$.
questions.answer: From $x=y$ and $x^2+y^2=8$: $2x^2=8 \Rightarrow x=\pm2$, giving points $(2,2)$ and $(-2,-2)$. $f(2,2)=4$ (maximum), $f(-2,-2)=-4$ (minimum).

questions.q: A farmer has 100 m of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river (no fence needed along the river side). If $x$ is the side parallel to the river and $y$ each perpendicular side, maximize the area $A=xy$ subject to $x+2y=100$.
questions.answer: $\nabla A=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle y,x\rangle=\lambda\langle1,2\rangle \Rightarrow y=\lambda,\ x=2\lambda \Rightarrow x=2y$. With $x+2y=100$: $2y+2y=100 \Rightarrow y=25$, $x=50$. Maximum area: $A=50(25)=1250$ m$^2$.

sections.heading: One more critical point and classification

questions.q: Find and classify the critical point(s) of $f(x,y)=x^2+xy+y^2$.
questions.answer: $f_x=2x+y=0$, $f_y=x+2y=0$. From the first, $y=-2x$; substituting: $x+2(-2x)=0 \Rightarrow -3x=0 \Rightarrow x=0$, $y=0$. $f_{xx}=2$, $f_{yy}=2$, $f_{xy}=1$; $D=4-1=3>0$ and $f_{xx}>0$, so $(0,0)$ is a local minimum.

questions.q: Minimize $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$ subject to $xy=1$ (with $x,y>0$).
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle2x,2y\rangle=\lambda\langle y,x\rangle \Rightarrow 2x=\lambda y,\ 2y=\lambda x$. Dividing: $\dfrac{2x}{2y}=\dfrac{\lambda y}{\lambda x} \Rightarrow x^2=y^2 \Rightarrow x=y$ (since both positive). With $xy=1$: $x^2=1 \Rightarrow x=y=1$. Minimum value: $f(1,1)=2$.

sections.heading: Global extrema on a closed region

questions.q: Find the maximum and minimum of $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$ on the closed disk $x^2+y^2\leq4$ (check both the interior critical point and the boundary).
questions.answer: Interior: $f_x=2x=0$, $f_y=2y=0 \Rightarrow (0,0)$, with $f(0,0)=0$ (a minimum). On the boundary $x^2+y^2=4$: $f=x^2+y^2=4$ everywhere on the boundary. So the minimum value is $0$ at $(0,0)$, and the maximum value is $4$, attained at every point on the boundary circle.

questions.q: A box with a square base of side $x$ and height $y$ has volume $V=x^2y=32$. Set up the Lagrange equations to minimize the surface area $S=2x^2+4xy$ subject to this constraint.
questions.answer: $\nabla S=\lambda\nabla g$ for $g=x^2y-32$: $\langle4x+4y,4x\rangle=\lambda\langle2xy,x^2\rangle$, together with $x^2y=32$.

questions.q: Solve the box problem above: find $x$ and $y$ that minimize $S=2x^2+4xy$ subject to $x^2y=32$.
questions.answer: From $4x=\lambda x^2$ (second component, $x\ne0$): $\lambda=\dfrac{4}{x}$. Substituting into the first: $4x+4y=\dfrac{4}{x}(2xy)=8y \Rightarrow 4x=4y \Rightarrow x=y$. With $x^2y=32$ and $y=x$: $x^3=32 \Rightarrow x=32^{1/3}=2\sqrt[3]{4}$, so $x=y=2\sqrt[3]{4}$.

questions.q: Find and classify the critical point(s) of $f(x,y)=4+x^3+y^3-3xy$.
questions.answer: $f_x=3x^2-3y=0 \Rightarrow y=x^2$. $f_y=3y^2-3x=0 \Rightarrow x=y^2$. Substituting: $x=(x^2)^2=x^4 \Rightarrow x^4-x=0 \Rightarrow x(x^3-1)=0 \Rightarrow x=0$ or $x=1$, giving $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$. $f_{xx}=6x$, $f_{yy}=6y$, $f_{xy}=-3$. At $(0,0)$: $D=0-9=-9<0$, a saddle point. At $(1,1)$: $D=36-9=27>0$, $f_{xx}=6>0$, a local minimum.

sections.heading: A Lagrange multiplier problem in three variables

questions.q: Set up the Lagrange equations to minimize $f(x,y,z)=x^2+y^2+z^2$ subject to $x+y+z=6$.
questions.answer: $\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g$: $\langle2x,2y,2z\rangle=\lambda\langle1,1,1\rangle \Rightarrow x=y=z=\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$, together with $x+y+z=6$.

questions.q: Solve the problem above.
questions.answer: Since $x=y=z$ and $x+y+z=6$: $3x=6 \Rightarrow x=y=z=2$. Minimum value: $f(2,2,2)=4+4+4=12$.
